findings: The merchant can collect a PaymentMethod with Payment Element or directly with a custom frontend. Stripe vaults details and forwarding accepts a PaymentMethod without Customer attachment. For a configured endpoint, the merchant server submits card object ID, exact URL, typed blank placeholders and replacement fields, plus the destination credentials on each API request. Stripe inserts vault card data and sends the outbound request, optionally applying Card Account Updater where enabled/available. It synchronously waits less than one minute for a third-party processor response, redacts identified PCI-sensitive data, stores the redacted response and relays a ForwardingRequest (old 18-28, 42-64, 245-249, 289-293, new 35-54, 68-87, 243-247, 288-292).

Vault and Forward does not confirm or capture PaymentIntents. The separate attempt on Stripe can cause duplicate capture after an external capture, and direct third-party authorization leaves refunds/disputes with that processor. Destination response and actual tokenization/authorization/capture/settlement are separate observations (old 28, 287-293, 756, new 54, 286-292, 734).

Link credentials are excluded and Link card payments should be routed to Stripe. A CVC expires with time or use, can be consumed by SetupIntent-confirmation validation, and may need re-collection if required. Google Pay FPAN uses standard card replacements and Google Pay DPAN uses network token replacements (old 30-40, 103-171, new 56-66, 114-182).

Both captures separate eligible forwarding destinations/countries from where a Stripe account may be registered. Setup needs test account IDs and production destination config. The general endpoint uses HTTPS and JSON/XML request/response and keeps hashed and encrypted versions of destination API keys. Keys shared for endpoint enablement are PGP-protected. The incoming request headers and body are encrypted and appear as encrypted_request in the Dashboard, and restricted forwarding write and optional read permissions serve different operations (old 355-365, 429-433, 558-562, 607-617, 710-720, 758-762, new 338-348, 420-424, 549-553, 598-608, 701-711, 736-740).

The `payment_method` parameter now explicitly accepts PaymentMethod, card-backed Source, Card and Issuing Card object IDs (old 42-49, new 68-75). This is a new explicit enumeration, without claiming the underlying implementation changed November 7.

November newly lists Apple Pay MPAN support, while retaining its DPAN-only detection and replacement descriptions (old 103-110 and 140-167, new 114-121 and 151-178). Treat this as a documented eligibility wording change with an unresolved integration detail.

contributions.original_prompts:
New raw `raw/stripe-payments-vault-and-forward-2026-11-07.md`. Prior raw `raw/stripe-vault-and-forward-2026.md`. Current summaries `wiki/sources/source-stripe-vault-and-forward.md`.

- Q1. For `https://docs.stripe.com/payments/vault-and-forward`, what documented behavior, prerequisites, actors and state transitions does the complete new capture establish? How do these compare with the matched prior capture and each mapped summary?

- Q2. Which changes are substantive, presentational or navigation-only? Identify the exact dated qualifications, conflicts and reciprocal routes that the proposed disposition should preserve.

reviewed_answers.Q1: The November 7 capture at https://docs.stripe.com/payments/vault-and-forward describes a business with a dedicated Stripe account team requesting access and configuring an allowed destination, subject to destination and Stripe-account-country boundaries. The merchant collects a PaymentMethod or otherwise references a permitted vault object. Its server sends the Stripe object ID, exact configured URL, typed empty card placeholders and replacements, and destination credentials. Stripe inserts the card data, automatically attempts a Card Account Updater refresh where enabled and available, sends the request, waits synchronously for the third-party response for less than a minute, redacts identified PCI-sensitive data, stores the redacted response and relays a ForwardingRequest. When a destination responds, even with 400, the guide illustrates forwarding HTTP 200 with downstream code and message in the body. The ForwardingRequest example separately shows response_details.status. The server must distinguish these from actual processor or vault outcome. Stripe does not confirm or capture a PaymentIntent in this flow, and the third-party processor handles refunds and disputes for its authorization. CVC may expire or be consumed, and Link credentials are excluded. May describes the same core mechanics with a general support contact; source-stripe-vault-and-forward.md still reflects that access wording and overstates the 200 response and the number of supported processors (old raw lines 14-40, old raw lines 245-293 and old raw lines 748-762, compared with new raw lines 31-66, new raw lines 243-292 and new raw lines 713-740).
reviewed_answers.Q2: For https://docs.stripe.com/payments/vault-and-forward, source-stripe-vault-and-forward.md needs a dated update. May 11 routes access to Stripe support and lists Apple Pay DPAN only. November 7 requires a dedicated account team, lists PaymentMethod, card-backed Source, Card and Issuing Card object IDs, and lists Apple Pay DPAN and MPAN even though its detection still says always DPAN and replacement instructions cover DPAN only (old raw lines 14-16, old raw lines 42-49, old raw lines 103-110 and old raw lines 140-167, versus new raw lines 31-33, new raw lines 68-75, new raw lines 114-121 and new raw lines 151-178). November adds Adyen v72 payments/storedPaymentMethods, Chase Orbital profile, an additional GMO endpoint and Yuno sandbox/live. Orchestration email request navigation is separate; the flow diagram and cURL/JSON changes illustrate rather than revise forwarding behavior. For destination selection, replace the baseline 30+ processors assertion in the source and catalog with dated exact endpoints and a separate configured own-vault route (old raw lines 367-427, new raw lines 350-418). Restore the pre-existing destination-response qualification on HTTP 200, retain the own-vault wording/example tension and the specialist support wording as dated, and preserve the reciprocal Vault and Forward concept and existing specialist and May raw routes (old raw lines 363-429 and old raw lines 748-762, new raw lines 346-420 and new raw lines 713-740).
